# Forking a site package

This page is for developers who want a site package of their own and would rather start from one that installs
than from an empty `package.xml`. It shows where the 7x packages come from, how to copy one, and what has to change so
your copy is a package of its own.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit the result by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth, so it reaches every installation through the setup wizard, the
kickstarter and ezupdate: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## Choose what to start from

| Start from | When | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `sevenx_multisite` | a site with demo content, several siteaccesses and languages, layouts | [se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage), `packages/sevenx_multisite/` |
| `sevenx_multisite_clean` | the same structure without the demo articles | same repository |
| `sevenx_site`, `sevenx_site_clean` | a simpler site | same repository |
| `cjw_multisite` | a fork that already replaced the demo content and the installer class: the best example of what a fork changes | [se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage) |

What each one installs is described in [sevenx_multisite](../sevenx-multisite/README.md) and
[cjw_multisite](../cjw-multisite/README.md).

## The source repository layout

Both repositories keep one folder per package below `packages/`; the folder name is the package name and the folder
holds what the `.ezpkg` archive will hold:

```text
packages/
├── build.sh                         (sevenx-ezpackage) packs every folder into <folder>.ezpkg
├── sevenx_multisite/
│   ├── package.xml                  the definition
│   ├── documents/LICENCE
│   ├── files/default/thumbnail/     the picture the setup wizard shows
│   ├── files/default/image/
│   └── settings/                    the installer files named in <settings>
├── sevenx_classes/
│   ├── package.xml
│   └── ezcontentclass/class-*.xml
└── sevenx_multisite_democontent/
    ├── package.xml
    ├── ezcontentclass/ ezcontentobject/ simplefiles/
    └── documents/LICENCE
bin/pack.sh, bin/repack_extension.sh, ant/createzpkg.sh
```

`cjw_multisite-ezpackage` has the same `bin/` and `ant/` scripts but no `packages/build.sh`; see
[Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md) for both ways of packing.

## Copy the repository

```bash
# on GitHub: Fork, or create an empty repository <your-org>/<yourname>-ezpackage
git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/<yourname>-ezpackage.git
cd <yourname>-ezpackage
# keep only the package folders you will change or ship
git mv packages/sevenx_multisite packages/acme_site
```

Keep the history: the 7x source repository goes back to 2006, and `git log -- packages/sevenx_multisite` explains
why most lines of the installer are there.

## Rename the package

The package name is what the index lists, what `kickstart.ini` names in `Site_package` and the directory the package
is imported into. Change it in `package.xml` and in the folder name together:

```xml
<package version="6.0.15-0" development="false" is_active="true" install_type="import">
  <name>acme_site</name>
  <summary>Acme starter site</summary>
  <description>What an editor gets after installing it.</description>
  <vendor>acme</vendor>
  <type value="site" />
  ...
</package>
```

| Field | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | lower-case letters, digits and `_` only; `eZPackage::isValidName()` accepts a name only if the `identifier` transformation leaves it unchanged | the upload page and `eZPackage::import()` refuse other names |
| `<name>` | unique: not the name of a 7x package | one name means one package to an installation: the kickstarter uses a package that is already imported instead of downloading it, the setup wizard in the browser removes an imported site package of that name and downloads it again, a required package of that name is kept when its version is high enough (`downloadAndImportPackage()` and `downloadDependantPackages()` in `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`), and an upload of an existing name is refused ("already exists") |
| `<vendor>` | your organization | the import puts the package in `var/storage/packages/<vendor>/`, the vendor turned into a directory name (`eZ systems` became `ez-systems`) |
| `<summary>` | one line | the setup wizard shows it under the thumbnail |
| `<maintainers>`, `<changelog>` | your names and a role address of your own | do not keep the 7x maintainer e-mail; reviewers and users write to it |
| `<packaging><host>` | your host or leave it as the kernel writes it | informational |

The full element list is on [The package.xml reference](../basics/package-xml-reference.md); the required fields on
[Fields package.xml cannot do without](../requirements/package-xml-required-fields.md).

## Rename the installer

The `<settings>` element lists PHP files of `settings/` that `CreateSites` includes with `include_once`:

```xml
<settings>
  <settings-file filename='ini-site.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='ini-admin.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='ini-common.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='acme-site-installer.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='install-scripts.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='roles.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='preferences.php'/>
</settings>
```

Rename the installer file and its class (`sevenxMultiSiteInstaller` became `cjwMultiSiteInstaller` in the CJW fork)
and update the small hook files that create it (`install-scripts.php`, `ini-site.php`, `roles.php` and the others each
call `new sevenxMultiSiteInstaller( ... )`). A class of your own name cannot collide with a 7x installer class, and the
debug output names your installer. Details: [Changing the installer script](changing-the-installer-script.md).

## Decide what to keep as a requirement

`<dependencies><requires>` names the packages installed before the site package:

```xml
<requires>
  <require type="ezpackage" name="sevenx_classes" min-version="5.1" />
  <require type="ezpackage" name="acme_site_democontent" min-version="1.0.0-1" />
</requires>
```

You can keep a 7x package as it is, as `cjw_multisite` keeps `sevenx_classes`, and replace only what you change. A
required package is looked up in the same `index.xml` as the site package, so your index must list it too (its `url`
may point at the 7x server). See [Declaring dependencies](../requirements/declaring-dependencies.md).

## Checklist

- [ ] Folder name, `<name>` and every reference to the old name changed.
- [ ] `<vendor>`, `<summary>`, `<description>`, maintainers and changelog are yours.
- [ ] Installer file and class renamed, hook files updated.
- [ ] `<requires>` lists exactly the packages you ship or reuse.
- [ ] Thumbnail replaced (`files/default/thumbnail/`), license file reviewed.
- [ ] Version reset for your first release ([Versioning your own packages](versioning-your-own-packages.md)).
